notes:
Context / quick history:
- Yesterday we ramped quantized variant v1.9 to 25% as part of cost experiment (expected ~20% token-cost reduction). Early alarms triggered for 'billing prompt' group (unexpected low pass rate).
- Two canonical failing examples pasted below (keep for reproduce).

Immediate hypotheses:
1) Quantization reduced model fidelity for certain numeric-verification patterns (likely 8-bit->4-bit path on some layers).
2) Prompt parsing edge-case: new tokenization change in compiler selects different token boundaries -> downstream classifier mismatch.
3) Runtime KV cache mismatch: rare stale KV entries cause alt completions under specific session prefix lengths (>512).

Quick checklist to triage (order matters):
- Reproduce locally with same seed + temperature as A/B (Kenji) -> deterministic check
- Run golden eval set (Sienna) with both models and prompt variants -> isolate prompt-sensitive failures
- Inspect tokenization diff (small tool) between v1.8.2 and v1.9 for example inputs (Marina)
- Capture KV cache traces for failing session lengths 600-1200 tokens (Kenji)
- Run small ablation: quantize only feedforward vs only attention to see where degradation shows up (eng-runtime)

Failing examples (sanitized):
1) "Invoice total 3/31/26: compute taxable amount for subtotal $13,470.23 with discount 2.5% and tax 8.25%" -> control correct numeric breakdown, treatment outputs rounded e.g. "13,000" (loss of precision / rounding).
2) "Given record id 0x7a3f2: return canonical slug and checksum" -> control returns stable slug, treatment returns alternate casing and missing checksum.

Notes on rollout strategy options:
A) Immediate rollback of v1.9 to 0% and create follow-up canary with logging (safe, higher cost)
B) Patch prompts: apply targeted prompt normalization for numeric patterns + route only billing-prompts to control variant (complicated to maintain)
C) Partial variant: keep v1.9 at 5% while we test quantization ablation (less disruption, slower measurement)
D) Runtime mitigation: enforce no-quantize for layers X,Y if ablation identifies them (requires infra change, release next week)

My preference: C for short-term (5%) + Kenji reproducible trace + Sienna prompt patch experiments. If numeric regressions still >5ppt in prompt subset, roll back fully.

Open questions to ask in 1:1:
- Do we have an historical fingerprint of similar numeric regressions tied to quantization (any incidents 2025-2026)? (Kenji/SRE)
- Can we ship a prompt-normalization shim at edge to normalize currency/number tokens without heavy product changes? (Product/SDK)
- Cost tolerance tradeoffs: is keeping higher-cost control acceptable for billing flow until next release? (PM/Finance)

Misc notes / scratch ideas:
- Add a lightweight "numeric-stability" unit test in evals harness that runs on PRs touching quantization kernels.
- Consider adding a feature flag to turn off aggressive token-merging heuristics for prompts with currency tokens.
- If rollback, create postmortem template with: timeline, root cause (quant vs tokenization vs cache), mitigation, follow-up fixes, owner, and rollout notes.
